questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Simple squamous epithelium, made of a single thin layer of flattened cells, is found in:

options.text: The walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs

solution.explanation: Squamous epithelium has flattened cells with irregular boundaries and forms thin linings where diffusion is important, such as the walls of blood vessels and the air sacs (alveoli) of lungs.
steps: Squamous → walls of blood vessels, air sacs of lungs
Columnar → lining of stomach and intestine
Cuboidal → ducts of glands, tubular parts of nephrons
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: The walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are an example of:

solution.explanation: Some columnar or cuboidal cells become specialised for secretion (glandular epithelium). A gland may be unicellular, made of isolated glandular cells such as the goblet cells of the alimentary canal, or multicellular, such as the salivary gland.
steps: Goblet cell = single secretory cell → unicellular gland
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: glandular epithelium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which features help to distinguish a male frog from a female frog?

options.text: Vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs
Webbed hind limbs and a nictitating membrane
A tympanum on each side of the head and bulged eyes
Moist slimy skin and dorsal green colour

solution.explanation: Male frogs have sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs. These are absent in female frogs.
steps: Male only → vocal sacs, copulatory pad
The other features are present in both sexes
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: morphology
solution.final_answer: Option A: Vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones.
Statement II: Ligaments attach one bone to another bone.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Tendons and ligaments are dense regular connective tissue, with collagen fibres in rows between parallel bundles of fibres. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and ligaments attach one bone to another. Both are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: dense connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (epithelium) with List-II (location).

List-I:
A. Ciliated epithelium
B. Compound epithelium
C. Cuboidal epithelium
D. Columnar epithelium

List-II:
I. Lining of stomach and intestine
II. Inner surface of fallopian tubes
III. Tubular parts of nephrons
IV. Moist surface of buccal cavity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each epithelium lines the surface whose function it suits.
steps: Ciliated → inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes (II)
Compound → moist surface of buccal cavity, pharynx, dry surface of skin (IV)
Cuboidal → ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons (III)
Columnar → lining of stomach and intestine (I)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Compound epithelium has a limited role in secretion and absorption.
Reason (R): Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Structure decides function in compound epithelium
solution.explanation: Because compound epithelium is multi-layered, substances cannot easily pass across it, so it has only a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. R is the reason for A.
steps: Multi-layered → poor secretion/absorption → A true and explained by R
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: compound epithelium
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Exocrine glands secrete all of the following EXCEPT:

solution.explanation: Exocrine glands release mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes and other cell products through ducts. Endocrine glands have no ducts and secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: glandular epithelium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cartilage cells (chondrocytes) are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix secreted by them.
Statement II: Bone has a soft and pliable ground substance that is poor in calcium salts.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In cartilage, the chondrocytes lie in small cavities in the matrix they secrete: Statement I is true. Bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, which gives it strength: Statement II is false. (Cartilage, not bone, has a pliable matrix.)
steps: Bone matrix hard, non-pliable, rich in calcium salts → II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: specialised connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the frog are correct?

(a) Frogs never drink water but absorb it through the skin.
(b) A frog has a distinct neck and a short tail.
(c) The forelimbs end in four digits and the hind limbs end in five digits.
(d) In water, the skin acts as an aquatic respiratory organ.
(e) The frog is a warm-blooded animal.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The frog absorbs water through its skin and uses the skin for respiration in water (cutaneous respiration). Its forelimbs end in four digits and the larger hind limbs in five. Its body is divided into head and trunk only, and it is cold-blooded (poikilotherm).
steps: (b) False: neck and tail are absent
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: morphology and anatomy

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Adipose tissue, which stores fats and is located mainly beneath the skin, is a type of:

solution.explanation: NCERT classifies connective tissue as loose, dense and specialised. Loose connective tissue includes areolar tissue and adipose tissue. Adipose cells store fats; excess nutrients are converted into fat and stored here.
steps: Loose connective tissue → areolar and adipose
Dense regular → tendons, ligaments; dense irregular → skin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: loose connective tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about muscle tissue are correct?

(a) Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends and do not show striations.
(b) Cardiac muscle cells have communication junctions (intercalated discs) that allow the cells to contract as a unit.
(c) Skeletal muscle fibres are involuntary.
(d) Smooth muscle is found in the walls of blood vessels, stomach and intestine.
(e) Cardiac muscle tissue is found in the heart and in the walls of large arteries.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform and unstriated, and line the walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine. Cardiac muscle is present only in the heart; intercalated discs let its cells contract as a unit. Skeletal muscle is attached to bones and is voluntary.
steps: (e) False: cardiac muscle is present only in the heart; artery walls have smooth muscle
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: muscle tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In female frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts.
Reason (R): In male frogs, the vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidneys and communicate with the urinogenital duct that opens into the cloaca.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In male frogs, the ureters carry both urine and sperms (urinogenital ducts), because the 10–12 vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidneys and reach the urinogenital duct. In female frogs, the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca. So A is false and R is true.
steps: Female frog: ureters and oviducts separate → A false
Male frog: vasa efferentia → kidney → urinogenital duct → cloaca → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: A applies the male arrangement to the female, which is the trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy, excretory and reproductive systems
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
Statement II: Gap junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue: Statement I is true. Cementing that keeps neighbouring cells together is done by adhering junctions; gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules: Statement II is false.
steps: Adhering → cementing; gap → cytoplasmic communication (II false)
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II gives the gap junction the function of the adhering junction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: cell junctions
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the frog is correct?

options.text: Its RBCs are nucleated and contain haemoglobin.
Twelve pairs of cranial nerves arise from its brain.
Its heart has two atria and two ventricles.
It excretes nitrogenous wastes mainly as uric acid.

solution.explanation: Frog blood has nucleated RBCs containing the red pigment haemoglobin. Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from its brain. The heart has three chambers (two atria and one ventricle), and the frog is ureotelic.
solution.why_others_wrong: The frog has ten pairs of cranial nerves, a three-chambered heart and is ureotelic; the other options change one of these numbers or terms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy (circulatory, neural and excretory systems)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Its RBCs are nucleated and contain haemoglobin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The most abundant protein in the animal world is:

solution.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world. RuBisCO (ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase) is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere.
solution.why_others_wrong: RuBisCO is the trap: it is the most abundant in the biosphere, not in the animal world.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', proteins

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Inulin is a polysaccharide made up of units of:

solution.explanation: Cellulose, starch and glycogen are polymers of glucose, while inulin is a polymer of fructose.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A nucleoside differs from a nucleotide in lacking a:

options.text: Pentose sugar and a phosphate group

solution.explanation: A nitrogen base attached to a sugar is a nucleoside (e.g. adenosine). When a phosphate group is also esterified to the sugar, it becomes a nucleotide (e.g. adenylic acid).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', biomacromolecules: nucleic acids and their building blocks

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Isomerases catalyse the linking together of two compounds.
Statement II: Hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C–C, C–halide or P–N bonds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Isomerases catalyse inter-conversion of optical, geometric or positional isomers; linking two compounds together is done by ligases: Statement I is false. Statement II is the NCERT description of hydrolases: true.
steps: Joining two compounds → ligases, not isomerases (I false)
Hydrolases → hydrolysis of these bonds (II true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Some nucleic acids behave like enzymes. These are called:

solution.explanation: Almost all enzymes are proteins, but some nucleic acids act as catalysts. These catalytic nucleic acids are called ribozymes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (protein) with List-II (function).

List-I:
A. Collagen
B. Trypsin
C. GLUT-4
D. Antibody

List-II:
I. Fights infectious agents
II. Intercellular ground substance
III. Enables glucose transport into cells
IV. Enzyme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Proteins carry out many functions: some transport nutrients across membranes, some fight infections, some are hormones and some are enzymes. NCERT tabulates these examples.
steps: GLUT-4 → enables glucose transport into cells (III)
solution.why_others_wrong: Wrong codes give collagen the enzyme role or swap GLUT-4 with antibody.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', proteins: some proteins and their functions
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Haemoglobin shows a quaternary structure.
Reason (R): Adult human haemoglobin consists of four subunits: two of α type and two of β type.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A protein has quaternary structure when it is an assembly of more than one polypeptide (subunit). Adult human haemoglobin has four subunits, 2α and 2β, so R is exactly why A is true.
steps: Quaternary structure = arrangement of several polypeptide subunits
Hb = 2α + 2β subunits → quaternary → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Lipids have molecular weights below 800 Da, yet they appear in the acid-insoluble fraction when a tissue is ground in trichloroacetic acid. This is because:

options.text: Their molecular weight exceeds 10,000 Da once they bind glycerol
On grinding, cell membranes break into pieces and form vesicles that are not water-soluble
They are polymers of fatty acids linked by peptide bonds
Trichloroacetic acid converts them into proteins

solution.explanation: Lipids are not strictly macromolecules. They come into the acid-insoluble fraction because, when the tissue is ground, the membranes (made largely of lipids) break into pieces and form vesicles that are not water-soluble, so they separate with the macromolecules.
steps: Lipids: molecular weight < 800 Da → not macromolecules
Grinding → membranes → water-insoluble vesicles → retained in the acid-insoluble fraction
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', biomacromolecules: acid-insoluble fraction
solution.final_answer: Option B: On grinding, cell membranes break into pieces and form vesicles that are not water-soluble

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about polysaccharides are correct?

(a) Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose.
(b) Starch can hold I₂ molecules in its helical portion and gives a blue colour.
(c) Cellulose gives a blue colour with iodine.
(d) In a polysaccharide chain such as glycogen, the right end is the reducing end and the left end is the non-reducing end.
(e) The exoskeleton of arthropods contains the complex polysaccharide chitin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Starch forms helical secondary structures that hold I₂ (starch–I₂ is blue). Cellulose lacks such complex helices, so it cannot hold I₂. Chitin, found in arthropod exoskeletons, is a complex polysaccharide.
steps: (c) False: cellulose has no complex helices to hold I₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Amino acids are substituted methanes.
Statement II: In glycine, the R group is a methyl group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In an amino acid, the α-carbon carries four substituents: hydrogen, a carboxyl group, an amino group and a variable R group, so amino acids are substituted methanes: Statement I is true. In glycine the R group is a hydrogen; a methyl group is the R group of alanine: Statement II is false.
steps: α-carbon with H, –COOH, –NH₂ and R → substituted methane (I true)
Glycine: R = H; alanine: R = CH₃; serine: R = hydroxymethyl (II false)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', biomacromolecules: amino acids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Malonate inhibits the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase because malonate:

options.text: Closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure and competes for the substrate-binding site
Removes the metal ion cofactor of the enzyme
Raises the activation energy of the uncatalysed reaction

solution.explanation: A competitive inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in molecular structure. It competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site, so the substrate cannot bind and enzyme action declines. Malonate inhibiting succinic dehydrogenase is the NCERT example.
steps: Inhibitor resembles substrate → binds the active site
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity (inhibitors)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure and competes for the substrate-binding site

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Low temperature preserves an enzyme in a temporarily inactive state.
Statement II: High temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Each enzyme works best at its optimum temperature. Below it the enzyme is only temporarily inactive and recovers on warming; well above it the protein is denatured and activity is destroyed. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Without an enzyme, about 200 molecules of H₂CO₃ are formed from CO₂ and H₂O in one hour. In the presence of carbonic anhydrase, about 600,000 molecules are formed every second. By roughly what factor has the enzyme increased the rate of the reaction?

solution.explanation: Compare both rates in the same unit of time before dividing.
steps: Catalysed: 600,000 per second × 3600 s = 2.16 × 10⁹ molecules per hour
solution.shortcut: 600,000 / 200 = 3000 per unit time; × 3600 for hours → seconds = 1.08 × 10⁷.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.0 × 10³ divides without converting the hour into seconds. 1.8 × 10⁵ takes an hour as 60 seconds. 0.83 divides the rates the wrong way round.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: chemical reactions and carbonic anhydrase

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (class of enzyme) with List-II (reaction catalysed).

List-I:
A. Oxidoreductases
B. Transferases
C. Lyases
D. Ligases

List-II:
I. Removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds
II. Linking together of two compounds, e.g. joining C–O, C–S, C–N or P–O bonds
III. Transfer of a group G (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates
IV. Oxidation-reduction between two substrates

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Read each List-II description for its key words: 'oxidation-reduction', 'transfer of a group', 'removal ... leaving double bonds', 'linking together of two compounds'.
steps: Lyases → removal of groups leaving double bonds (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: The usual error is to swap lyases (which remove groups) with ligases (which join compounds).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about co-factors are correct?

(a) Haem is the prosthetic group in the enzymes peroxidase and catalase.
(b) The co-enzymes NAD and NADP contain the vitamin niacin.
(c) Zinc is a co-factor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.
(d) Co-enzymes are permanently and tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
(e) Removal of the co-factor does not affect the catalytic activity of the enzyme.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Co-factors: prosthetic groups, co-enzymes and metal ions
solution.explanation: Prosthetic groups (such as haem) are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. Co-enzymes are bound only transiently, usually during catalysis, and many contain vitamins. Some enzymes need metal ions (e.g. zinc for carboxypeptidase). When the co-factor is removed, catalytic activity is lost.
steps: (e) False: activity is lost without the co-factor
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) gives co-enzymes the tight binding that defines prosthetic groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: co-factors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In proteins, only right-handed helices are observed.
Reason (R): The primary structure of a protein is the sequence of amino acids in it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Primary and secondary structure of proteins
solution.explanation: NCERT states that the protein thread may be folded as a helix and that only right-handed helices are seen in proteins: A is true. The primary structure is the amino acid sequence: R is true. But the definition of primary structure says nothing about the handedness of the helix, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: secondary structure, right-handed helices only → true
R: primary structure = amino acid sequence → true
R is about a different level of structure → not the reason
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following amino acids is correctly matched with its nature?

solution.concept: Classification of amino acids by the R group
solution.explanation: The R group decides the nature of an amino acid. NCERT gives: acidic – glutamic acid; basic – lysine; neutral – valine; aromatic – tyrosine, phenylalanine, tryptophan.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong pair gives the amino acid the nature of another one in the NCERT list.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', biomacromolecules: amino acids

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In humans, the trachea divides into the right and left primary bronchi at the level of the:

solution.explanation: The trachea is a straight tube extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity, where it divides at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra into the right and left primary bronchi.
steps: Division into primary bronchi → level of 5th thoracic vertebra
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', human respiratory system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Insects exchange gases with the atmosphere through:

solution.explanation: Lower invertebrates such as sponges, coelenterates and flatworms use simple diffusion over the body surface; earthworms use their moist cuticle; insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) that carry air into the body.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory organs
solution.final_answer: Option B: A network of tracheal tubes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The conducting part of the human respiratory system extends from the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles.
Statement II: The alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are the NCERT division of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports air to the alveoli, clears it of foreign particles, humidifies it and brings it to body temperature. The exchange part is where O₂ and CO₂ actually diffuse between blood and air.
steps: External nostrils → terminal bronchioles = conducting part (I true)
Alveoli and their ducts = exchange part (II true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', human respiratory system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The respiratory rhythm centre, which is primarily responsible for regulating breathing, is located in the:

solution.explanation: A specialised centre in the medulla region of the brain, the respiratory rhythm centre, is primarily responsible for this regulation. The pneumotaxic centre in the pons can moderate it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The pons holds the pneumotaxic centre, which only moderates the rhythm centre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', regulation of respiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: Medulla region of the brain

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A healthy man has a tidal volume of 500 mL, an inspiratory reserve volume of 3000 mL, an expiratory reserve volume of 1100 mL and a residual volume of 1200 mL. His expiratory capacity is:

solution.explanation: Expiratory capacity (EC) is the total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration: the tidal volume plus the expiratory reserve volume.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2300 mL is ERV + RV, the functional residual capacity. 3500 mL is TV + IRV, the inspiratory capacity. 4600 mL is TV + IRV + ERV, the vital capacity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory volumes and capacities

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Inspiration takes place when the intra-pulmonary pressure is less than the atmospheric pressure.
Reason (R): During inspiration, the external inter-costal muscles relax.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Pressure gradient and muscles of breathing
solution.explanation: Air moves in when there is a negative pressure in the lungs relative to the atmosphere: A is true. Inspiration starts with contraction of the diaphragm, and contraction (not relaxation) of the external inter-costal muscles lifts the ribs and sternum, enlarging the thoracic chamber: R is false.
steps: Intra-pulmonary pressure < atmospheric → air rushes in → A true
External inter-costals contract during inspiration → R false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', mechanism of breathing
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about transport of gases in humans are correct?

(a) About 97 per cent of O₂ is transported by RBCs in the blood.
(b) About 70 per cent of CO₂ is carried as bicarbonate.
(c) About 20–25 per cent of CO₂ is carried by haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin.
(d) Each haemoglobin molecule can carry a maximum of two molecules of O₂.
(e) About 7 per cent of CO₂ is carried in a dissolved state through plasma.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: About 97% of O₂ travels with RBCs and 3% dissolved in plasma. Of CO₂, 20–25% is carried as carbamino-haemoglobin, about 70% as bicarbonate and about 7% dissolved in plasma. Each haemoglobin molecule can carry up to four O₂ molecules.
steps: (d) False: maximum four O₂ per haemoglobin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of gases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Compared with oxygen, the solubility of carbon dioxide is about:

solution.explanation: Solubility of the gases and the thickness of the membranes also affect diffusion. CO₂ is 20–25 times more soluble than O₂, so the amount of CO₂ that can diffuse per unit difference in partial pressure is much higher than that of O₂.
steps: Solubility of CO₂ ≈ 20–25 × that of O₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', exchange of gases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged, so the respiratory surface decreases.
Statement II: Asthma is a difficulty in breathing, causing wheezing, due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements match NCERT. In emphysema the damaged alveolar walls reduce the respiratory surface; cigarette smoking is a major cause. In asthma, inflamed bronchi and bronchioles make breathing difficult and cause wheezing.
steps: Asthma → inflamed bronchi and bronchioles (II true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', disorders of the respiratory system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Under normal physiological conditions, every 100 mL of oxygenated blood delivers about 5 mL of O₂ to the tissues. If 5 L of blood flows through the tissues every minute, the volume of O₂ delivered to the tissues per minute is about:

solution.explanation: Find how many 100 mL portions are in 5 L of blood, then multiply by the 5 mL of O₂ each portion delivers.
steps: O₂ delivered = 50 × 5 mL = 250 mL per minute
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 mL uses the 4 mL figure, which is for CO₂ delivered to the alveoli. 25 mL and 2500 mL come from slipping a factor of 10 while converting litres to 100 mL portions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of oxygen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): More CO₂ binds to haemoglobin in the tissues than in the alveoli.
Reason (R): In the tissues pCO₂ is high and pO₂ is low, which favours the binding of CO₂ to haemoglobin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: CO₂ binding to haemoglobin depends on partial pressures. Where pCO₂ is high and pO₂ is low (tissues), more CO₂ binds; where pCO₂ is low and pO₂ is high (alveoli), CO₂ is released. So R is the reason for A.
steps: Tissues: high pCO₂, low pO₂ → binding favoured
Alveoli: low pCO₂, high pO₂ → dissociation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of carbon dioxide
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the regulation of respiration are correct?

(a) The pneumotaxic centre in the pons can reduce the duration of inspiration and thereby alter the respiratory rate.
(b) A chemosensitive area adjacent to the rhythm centre is highly sensitive to CO₂ and hydrogen ions.
(c) Receptors associated with the aortic arch and carotid artery can recognise changes in CO₂ and H⁺ concentration.
(d) Oxygen plays a major role in the regulation of the respiratory rhythm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Chemical and neural control of breathing
solution.explanation: The pneumotaxic centre moderates the rhythm centre. Rising CO₂ and H⁺ activate the chemosensitive area and the receptors in the aortic arch and carotid artery, which signal the rhythm centre to adjust breathing. NCERT states that the role of oxygen in regulating the respiratory rhythm is quite insignificant.
steps: (d) False: the role of O₂ is quite insignificant
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) is the trap: breathing is driven mainly by CO₂ and H⁺, not by O₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', regulation of respiration

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (partial pressure) with List-II (value in mm Hg).

List-I:
A. pO₂ in atmospheric air
B. pO₂ in oxygenated blood
C. pCO₂ in deoxygenated blood
D. pCO₂ in atmospheric air

List-II:
I. 0.3
II. 45
III. 95
IV. 159

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT tabulates partial pressures (mm Hg) at different sites. O₂ falls from the atmosphere to the tissues; CO₂ is almost absent in atmospheric air and highest in tissues and deoxygenated blood.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', exchange of gases: partial pressures of O₂ and CO₂
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The most abundant type of white blood cell (leucocyte) in human blood is the:

solution.explanation: Neutrophils are the most abundant leucocytes (60–65% of total WBCs). Basophils are the least (0.5–1%).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: formed elements

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which part of the human heart initiates and maintains its rhythmic contractile activity and is therefore called the pacemaker?

solution.explanation: The sino-atrial node (SAN) generates the maximum number of action potentials (70–75 per minute), so it starts and maintains the rhythm of the heart. It is called the pacemaker.
steps: SAN → highest rate of action potentials → pacemaker
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human circulatory system: nodal tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: If a person's heart beats 75 times per minute, the duration of one cardiac cycle is:

solution.explanation: One heartbeat is one cardiac cycle, so the duration of a cycle is 60 seconds divided by the number of beats per minute.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.25 s divides the wrong way (75/60). 0.75 s divides 75 by 100 instead of 60 by 75. 0.08 s is a decimal slip.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Plasma proteins constitute about 20–25 per cent of plasma.
Statement II: Albumins help in osmotic balance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Plasma is 90–92% water and proteins make up only 6–8% of it: Statement I is false. Of the plasma proteins, fibrinogen is needed for clotting, globulins for defence and albumins for osmotic balance: Statement II is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: plasma
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A closed circulatory system, in which blood always flows through a closed network of vessels, is found in:

solution.explanation: Arthropods (including insects) and molluscs have an open circulatory system: blood is pumped into open spaces or sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', circulatory pathways

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature of a standard ECG) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. P-wave
B. QRS complex
C. T-wave
D. End of the T-wave

List-II:
I. End of systole
II. Depolarisation of the atria
III. Return of the ventricles from excited to normal state
IV. Depolarisation of the ventricles

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each peak of the ECG matches an electrical event in the heart.
steps: P-wave → depolarisation of the atria, which causes atrial contraction (II)
QRS complex → depolarisation of the ventricles, which starts ventricular contraction (IV)
T-wave → return of the ventricles from excited to normal state, i.e. repolarisation (III)
End of the T-wave → end of systole (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: The common mistake gives the P-wave to the ventricles or the T-wave to depolarisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', electrocardiograph (ECG)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An Rh-ve mother carrying an Rh+ve foetus in a subsequent pregnancy may have a baby with erythroblastosis foetalis.
Reason (R): During the delivery of her first Rh+ve child, the mother may be exposed to small amounts of foetal Rh+ve blood and start preparing antibodies against the Rh antigen.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the first pregnancy the placenta keeps the two bloods apart. At the first delivery, some foetal Rh+ve blood may reach the mother, who then makes anti-Rh antibodies. In later pregnancies these antibodies can leak into the Rh+ve foetus and destroy its RBCs (erythroblastosis foetalis). R explains A.
steps: Next Rh+ve foetus → maternal antibodies destroy foetal RBCs (A true)
R is the cause of A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood groups: Rh grouping
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about coagulation of blood are correct?

(a) An enzyme complex, thrombokinase, is required for the formation of thrombin from prothrombin.
(b) Thrombin converts inactive fibrinogen in the plasma into fibrin.
(c) Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
(d) An injury stimulates the platelets to release certain factors that activate the mechanism of coagulation.
(e) Serum is plasma that still contains the clotting factors.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The clot is a network of fibrin threads in which formed elements are trapped. Fibrin forms from fibrinogen under thrombin, and thrombin forms from prothrombin with the help of thrombokinase. Platelets release factors after an injury, and Ca²⁺ is essential. Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.
steps: (e) False: serum is plasma without clotting factors
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', coagulation of blood; plasma

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) of the human heart is located in the:

options.text: Upper right corner of the right atrium
Lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum
Wall of the left ventricle near the apex
Upper part of the inter-ventricular septum

solution.explanation: The SAN lies in the upper right corner of the right atrium. The AVN lies in the lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum. From the AVN, the bundle of His passes through the atrio-ventricular septum to the top of the inter-ventricular septum.
steps: SAN → upper right corner of right atrium
AVN → lower left corner of right atrium, near AV septum
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option is the position of the SAN; the inter-ventricular septum carries the bundle of His and its branches.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human circulatory system: nodal tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: Lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The first heart sound, 'lub', is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves.
Statement II: The second heart sound, 'dub', is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: During each cardiac cycle two prominent sounds are heard. The first (lub) comes from closure of the atrio-ventricular valves (tricuspid and bicuspid) at the start of ventricular systole; the second (dub) from closure of the semilunar valves at the start of ventricular diastole. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the hepatic portal system, the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the:

solution.explanation: A unique vascular connection exists between the digestive tract and the liver. The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it is delivered to the systemic circulation.
steps: Intestine → hepatic portal vein → liver → systemic circulation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', double circulation: hepatic portal system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Intestine to the liver

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Parasympathetic neural signals to the heart:

options.text: Increase the strength of ventricular contraction
Have no effect, because the heart is myogenic
Decrease the rate of heartbeat and the speed of conduction of action potential, and thereby the cardiac output

solution.explanation: The heart is myogenic (auto-regulated by nodal tissue), but a centre in the medulla oblongata can moderate it through the ANS. Sympathetic signals increase heart rate, strength of ventricular contraction and cardiac output; parasympathetic signals decrease heart rate, conduction speed and cardiac output.
steps: Parasympathetic → decreases rate, conduction speed, output
solution.why_others_wrong: The first two are sympathetic effects. Being myogenic does not stop the ANS from moderating the heart.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', regulation of cardiac activity
solution.final_answer: Option D: Decrease the rate of heartbeat and the speed of conduction of action potential, and thereby the cardiac output

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At rest, a person's stroke volume is 70 mL and heart rate 72 beats per minute. During exercise, the stroke volume rises to 80 mL and the heart rate to 90 beats per minute. By how much does the cardiac output increase?

solution.concept: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate
solution.explanation: Work out the cardiac output in each state and subtract.
steps: At rest: 70 mL × 72 = 5040 mL per minute
During exercise: 80 mL × 90 = 7200 mL per minute
solution.why_others_wrong: 7200 and 5040 mL are the two outputs themselves, not the increase. 1260 mL multiplies only the rise in heart rate (18) by the resting stroke volume and ignores the larger stroke volume.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle: stroke volume and cardiac output

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (leucocyte) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Basophils
B. Eosinophils
C. Monocytes
D. Lymphocytes

List-II:
I. Occur as B and T forms responsible for immune responses
II. Phagocytic cells forming 6–8 per cent of WBCs
III. Secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin
IV. Resist infections and are associated with allergic reactions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes, monocytes) have distinct roles.
steps: Basophils → histamine, serotonin, heparin; inflammatory reactions (III)
Lymphocytes → B and T forms, immune responses (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping basophils and eosinophils is the classic error; both are granulocytes linked with allergy and inflammation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: formed elements
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Amphibians and most reptiles show incomplete double circulation.
Reason (R): Their heart has a single ventricle into which both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood flow and get mixed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) have a three-chambered heart. The left atrium receives oxygenated blood and the right atrium deoxygenated blood, but both empty into the single ventricle, which pumps out mixed blood. That mixing is why the double circulation is incomplete, so R explains A.
steps: Two atria, one ventricle → mixing in the ventricle
Mixed blood pumped out → incomplete double circulation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', circulatory pathways
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about disorders of the circulatory system are correct?

(a) Repeated blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher indicate hypertension.
(b) In coronary artery disease, deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue narrow the lumen of the arteries supplying the heart muscle.
(c) Angina occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
(d) Heart failure is the same as cardiac arrest.
(e) Heart failure is sometimes called congestive heart failure because congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg; repeated readings of 140/90 or higher indicate hypertension. CAD (atherosclerosis) narrows the coronary arteries. Angina is acute chest pain when too little oxygen reaches the heart muscle. Heart failure means the heart does not pump blood effectively enough; it is not the same as cardiac arrest (heart stops beating) or a heart attack (heart muscle suddenly damaged by inadequate blood supply).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', disorders of circulatory system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During joint diastole, all four chambers are relaxed and the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open.
Statement II: Atrial systole accounts for about 70 per cent of the filling of the ventricles.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: At the start of the cycle all four chambers are in joint diastole: the AV valves are open, blood flows from the atria into the ventricles, and the semilunar valves are closed. Statement I is true. Most ventricular filling takes place in this phase; atrial systole then increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by only about 30 per cent. Statement II is false.
steps: Joint diastole: AV valves open, semilunar valves closed → I true
Atrial systole adds about 30% of ventricular filling, not 70% → II false
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT gives about 30 per cent for the increase due to atrial systole; Statement II inflates it, so options A and B fail.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following groups of animals is uricotelic?

options.text: Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects

solution.explanation: Uricotelic animals excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid in pellet or paste form with minimum loss of water: reptiles, birds, land snails and insects.
steps: Ammonotelic → bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, aquatic insects
Ureotelic → mammals, many terrestrial amphibians, marine fishes
Uricotelic → reptiles, birds, land snails, insects
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', introduction: modes of excretion
solution.final_answer: Option C: Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The notch at the centre of the inner concave surface of the kidney, through which the ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter, is called the:

solution.explanation: Towards the centre of the inner concave surface of each kidney is a notch called the hilum. Inner to the hilum is a broad funnel-shaped space, the renal pelvis, with projections called calyces.
steps: Notch on inner concave surface → hilum
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human kidney, the columns of Bertini are:

options.text: Extensions of the cortex between the medullary pyramids
Bundles of collecting ducts in the renal papillae

solution.explanation: The medulla is divided into a few conical masses, the medullary pyramids, which project into the calyces. The cortex extends in between the medullary pyramids as renal columns called columns of Bertini.
steps: Medullary pyramids → conical masses of medulla
Columns of Bertini → cortex extending between pyramids
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system
solution.final_answer: Option B: Extensions of the cortex between the medullary pyramids

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The Malpighian corpuscle, PCT and DCT of the nephron are situated in the cortical region of the kidney.
Statement II: Each human kidney has nearly one million nephrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT facts. Each kidney has nearly one million nephrons, the functional units. The Malpighian corpuscle, PCT and DCT lie in the cortex, while the loop of Henle dips into the medulla.
steps: About one million nephrons per kidney (II true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system: nephron
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The glomerular filtration rate of a healthy person is 125 mL per minute. If exactly 99 per cent of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules, the volume of urine formed in one day is:

solution.explanation: Convert the GFR to a daily volume, then keep only the 1 per cent that is not reabsorbed.
steps: Filtrate per day = 125 mL × 60 × 24 = 180,000 mL = 180 L
solution.shortcut: NCERT's 180 L of filtrate per day is worth remembering; 1% of it is 1.8 L.
solution.why_others_wrong: 180 L is the filtrate, before reabsorption. 18 L keeps 10% instead of 1%. 0.18 L keeps 0.1%.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The ascending limb of Henle's loop is impermeable to water.
Reason (R): The ascending limb of Henle's loop allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements about the ascending limb, so both are true. But transport of electrolytes does not explain why the limb is impermeable to water; these are two separate properties. Together they make the filtrate dilute as it moves up into the cortex.
steps: R: electrolytes move out actively or passively → true
R does not explain the water impermeability
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A wrongly treats one property of the ascending limb as the cause of the other.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the nephron) with List-II (function).

List-I:
A. Proximal convoluted tubule
B. Descending limb of loop of Henle
C. Distal convoluted tubule
D. Collecting duct

List-II:
I. Allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium
II. Conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water
III. Permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes
IV. Reabsorbs nearly all essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each segment of the nephron handles water and solutes differently.
steps: PCT → nearly all nutrients, 70–80% of electrolytes and water (IV)
Descending limb → permeable to water, almost impermeable to electrolytes (III)
DCT → conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water (II)
Collecting duct → passes small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium (I)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart causes the release of atrial natriuretic factor (ANF). ANF causes:

options.text: Vasoconstriction and a rise in blood pressure
Release of renin from the JG cells
Vasodilation and a fall in blood pressure

solution.concept: ANF as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism
solution.explanation: ANF causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels) and thereby decreases blood pressure. So the ANF mechanism acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism.
steps: More blood to atria → ANF released
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options describe the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone mechanism, which ANF opposes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function
solution.final_answer: Option C: Vasodilation and a fall in blood pressure

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about glomerular filtration are correct?

(a) The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood.
(b) Blood is filtered through three layers: the endothelium of the glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman's capsule and a basement membrane between them.
(c) The podocytes of Bowman's capsule leave minute spaces called filtration slits.
(d) Plasma proteins pass freely into the lumen of Bowman's capsule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries forces fluid through the three-layered filtration membrane. The podocytes are arranged to leave filtration slits. Filtration is so fine that almost all constituents of plasma except the proteins pass into Bowman's capsule, so it is called ultrafiltration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In haemodialysis, an anticoagulant such as heparin is added to the blood before it is pumped into the dialysing unit.
Statement II: Glomerulonephritis is the formation of stones or insoluble masses of crystallised salts in the kidney.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: During haemodialysis, blood drained from an artery is mixed with heparin and pumped through the dialysing unit; anti-heparin is added before it is returned: Statement I is true. Glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the glomeruli; stone formation is renal calculi: Statement II is false.
steps: Heparin added before dialysis → I true
Glomerulonephritis = inflamed glomeruli; stones = renal calculi → II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', disorders of the excretory system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Human kidneys can produce urine nearly four times as concentrated as the initial filtrate.
Reason (R): The counter-current mechanism maintains an osmolarity gradient in the medullary interstitium, from about 300 mOsmol L⁻¹ in the cortex to about 1200 mOsmol L⁻¹ in the inner medulla.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle's loop and of blood in the two limbs of the vasa recta is in opposite directions. This keeps the medullary interstitium increasingly concentrated towards the inner medulla. Water then passes easily out of the collecting tubule into this hyperosmotic interstitium, concentrating the urine. R explains A (1200/300 = 4).
steps: Water leaves collecting duct → urine concentrated
Maximum concentration ≈ 4 × filtrate → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', mechanism of concentration of the filtrate
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the renin-angiotensin mechanism are correct?

(a) A fall in glomerular blood flow or GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin.
(b) Renin converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II.
(c) Angiotensin II is a powerful vasodilator.
(d) Angiotensin II activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
(e) Aldosterone causes reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from the distal parts of the tubule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: When GFR falls, the juxtaglomerular apparatus releases renin. The resulting angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor: it raises glomerular blood pressure and thereby GFR. It also makes the adrenal cortex release aldosterone, which increases Na⁺ and water reabsorption, raising blood pressure and GFR.
steps: (c) False: angiotensin II is a vasoconstrictor
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) is the trap: vasodilation is the effect of ANF, which works against this mechanism.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (excretory structure) with List-II (animal).

List-I:
A. Antennal glands
B. Malpighian tubules
C. Nephridia
D. Protonephridia

List-II:
I. Earthworm
II. Amphioxus
III. Prawn
IV. Cockroach

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT names the excretory structure of each group. The trap is Amphioxus, a cephalochordate that, like flatworms, has protonephridia.
steps: Antennal (green) glands → crustaceans such as prawn (III)
Malpighian tubules → most insects including cockroach (IV)
Protonephridia (flame cells) → flatworms, rotifers, some annelids and Amphioxus (II)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', introduction: excretory structures
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is present in juxtamedullary nephrons but is absent or highly reduced in cortical nephrons?

options.text: A short loop of Henle and a well-developed vasa recta
A proximal convoluted tubule with a brush border
A long loop of Henle running deep into the medulla, with a well-developed vasa recta

solution.explanation: In most nephrons (cortical nephrons) the loop of Henle is short and extends only a little into the medulla, and the vasa recta is absent or highly reduced. Juxtamedullary nephrons have a very long loop of Henle that runs deep into the medulla and a prominent vasa recta, a U-shaped vessel parallel to the loop.
steps: Cortical nephron → short loop, vasa recta absent or reduced
Juxtamedullary nephron → long loop, vasa recta well developed
Glomerulus and PCT → present in all nephrons
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option pairs a short loop (a cortical feature) with a juxtamedullary feature. The glomerulus and PCT are common to all nephrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system: nephron
solution.final_answer: Option D: A long loop of Henle running deep into the medulla, with a well-developed vasa recta

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In humans, ciliary movement is responsible for:

options.text: The movement of macrophages and leucocytes
The passage of ova through the female reproductive tract

solution.explanation: Ciliary movement occurs in internal tubular organs lined by ciliated epithelium. Coordinated cilia in the trachea remove dust particles, and ciliary movement helps the passage of ova through the female reproductive tract.
solution.why_others_wrong: Macrophages and leucocytes show amoeboid movement; jaws and heart move by muscular movement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', types of movement
solution.final_answer: Option D: The passage of ova through the female reproductive tract

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The total number of bones in the human skull, including the cranial and facial bones, is:

solution.explanation: The skull has two sets of bones, cranial and facial, totalling 22. The 8 cranial bones form the hard protective outer covering of the brain; the 14 facial bones form the front part of the skull.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 and 14 are the cranial and facial bones alone; 26 is the number of vertebrae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system: axial skeleton

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The joint between the atlas and the axis vertebrae is a:

solution.explanation: Synovial joints allow considerable movement. NCERT examples: ball and socket (humerus–pectoral girdle), hinge (knee), pivot (atlas–axis), gliding (between carpals), saddle (carpal–metacarpal of thumb).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', joints

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Gout is caused by:

options.text: Accumulation of uric acid crystals in the joints
An auto-immune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction
An age-related decrease in bone mass

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Each upper limb and each lower limb of a human contains 30 bones. Each half of the pectoral girdle is made of a clavicle and a scapula, and the pelvic girdle is made of two coxal bones (each formed by the fusion of ilium, ischium and pubis). The total number of bones in the appendicular skeleton is:

solution.explanation: Add the bones of the four limbs and of the two girdles, counting each fused coxal bone as one bone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the A-band shortens.
Reason (R): Muscle contraction takes place by the sliding of thin filaments over thick filaments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: When the thin (actin) filaments slide over the thick (myosin) filaments, the Z-lines are pulled closer and the sarcomere shortens. The I-bands get reduced, but the A-bands, which correspond to the thick filaments, retain their length: A is false. R is the sliding filament theory: true.
steps: I-band reduces; A-band retains its length → A false
R is the NCERT mechanism → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Students often think every band shortens; NCERT states that the I-bands get reduced while the A-bands retain their length.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of a sarcomere) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. I-band
B. A-band
C. Z-line
D. M-line

List-II:
I. Thin fibrous membrane holding the thick filaments together in the middle of the A-band
II. Elastic fibre that bisects the I-band; thin filaments are firmly attached to it
III. Light band containing actin (isotropic band)
IV. Dark band containing myosin (anisotropic band)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alternate light and dark bands give skeletal muscle its striated look.
steps: Z-line → bisects I-band, anchors thin filaments (II)
M-line → holds thick filaments in middle of A-band (I)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal muscle: structure of the myofibril
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the mechanism of muscle contraction are correct?

(a) Acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
(b) The action potential spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of Ca²⁺ into the sarcoplasm.
(c) The myosin head binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.
(d) During relaxation, Ca²⁺ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
(e) The Ca²⁺ that triggers contraction is released from the mitochondria of the muscle fibre.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A neural signal releases acetylcholine at the motor end plate, generating an action potential in the sarcolemma. Ca²⁺ is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, the store of calcium ions, and binds troponin, exposing the active sites on actin for myosin heads. Cross bridges form and pull actin. During relaxation Ca²⁺ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
steps: (e) False: the Ca²⁺ comes from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, not mitochondria
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The first seven pairs of ribs are called true ribs.
Statement II: The 11th and 12th pairs of ribs are called vertebrochondral (false) ribs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The first seven pairs join the sternum ventrally through hyaline cartilage: true ribs. The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage instead: vertebrochondral (false) ribs. The 11th and 12th pairs are not connected ventrally: floating ribs. So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system: rib cage
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the human vertebral column is correct?

options.text: It is formed by 33 separate vertebrae in the adult
It is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae

solution.explanation: The vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged vertebrae and is dorsally placed. The vertebral formula is cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacral 1 (fused) and coccygeal 1 (fused).
solution.why_others_wrong: 12 is the thoracic count and 7 the cervical count; the sacral and coccygeal vertebrae are fused, so NCERT counts 26 units.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system: vertebral column
solution.final_answer: Option D: It is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Tetany is characterised by rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle.
Reason (R): Tetany is caused by a high level of Ca²⁺ in body fluids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Tetany is rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle: A is true. It is due to low, not high, Ca²⁺ in body fluid: R is false.
steps: A matches the NCERT definition → true
Cause is low Ca²⁺ → R false
solution.why_others_wrong: Linking Ca²⁺ with contraction tempts students to accept 'high Ca²⁺' as the cause.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', disorders of muscular and skeletal system
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:

B. Hinge joint

D. Saddle joint

I. Knee joint
II. Between humerus and pectoral girdle
III. Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb
IV. Between the carpals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Gliding and saddle joints are both in the hand, which is the trap: gliding joints are between the carpals; the saddle joint is between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb.
steps: Ball and socket → humerus and pectoral girdle (II)
